TI Comparative analysis of somatotype indicators and performance rates in
   cadets engaged in kettlebell lifting
SO PHYSICAL EDUCATION OF STUDENTS
LA English
DT Article
DE kettlebell sport; somatotype; bioimpedance method; indices; performance
ID PHYSICAL DEVELOPMENT; BODY-COMPOSITION; COMBAT SPORTS
AB Background and Study Aim. The bioimpedance method is used to evaluate body composition due to its objectivity, non-invasiveness, and ease of use at various levels. Its application helps establish the relationship between body composition and physical performance, predict competitive success, and assess training efficiency. This method is widely used in strength sports. The aim of this study was to compare the somatotype indicators of cadets engaged in kettlebell lifting with their actual competitive performance. Materials and Methods. Sixty-two kettlebell lifting athletes, all cadets at military academies, were divided into two groups. Group 1 included 42 athletes aged 20.67 +/- 0.39 years, with competitive levels ranging from beginner to first-class athlete. Group 2 consisted of 20 athletes, with a mean age of 22.20 +/- 0.54 years. Their competitive level ranged from national- to international-level competitors (Candidate for Master of Sports, Master of Sports, and International-Class Master of Sports). The age difference between the groups was statistically significant (p < 0.05). Body height and body mass, body fat percentage (%), muscle mass percentage (%), visceral fat level (%), and basal metabolic rate (kcal) were measured. Total muscle mass (kg), fat mass (kg), body mass index (BMI), fat-free mass index (FFMI), skeletal muscle mass index (SMI), and performance index were calculated. To characterize the data, the median and the 1st (25th) and 3rd (75th) quartiles were determined. The significance of differences between groups was assessed using Rosenbaum's nonparametric criterion (Q) and the information measure of correlation (I) between the analyzed characteristics. Results. Most somatotype indicators showed similar values in both groups. Most participants had a body fat percentage above the average range and a muscle mass percentage within the average range. Most participants also had a BMI above the average range, an FFMI below the average range, and a high SMI. A significant increase in the performance index was observed in Group 2 (Q = 13, p < 0.05). A significant predominance of individuals with below-average FFMI was found in Group 1 (2I = 67.54, p < 0.01). Quartile ranges were established for the evaluated indices in kettlebell athletes. A performance index value of 155-209 was observed within the interquartile range for Group 1, whereas for Group 2 this range was 238-358. The interquartile range for FFMI was 16-18 kg/m & sup2; in Group 1 and 16-17 kg/m & sup2; in Group 2. The interquartile range for SMI was 8.1-9.2 kg/m & sup2; in Group 1 and 8.2-9.0 kg/m & sup2; in Group 2. Conclusions. Competitive performance differed significantly between the groups, whereas most somatotype indicators showed similar values. Quartile ranges were established for the performance index, FFMI, and SMI in kettlebell athletes. The bioimpedance-derived indices used in this study can be applied to characterize the somatotype features of kettlebell athletes and to compare athletes with different levels of competitive performance.

TI Narrative inquiry and educational policies: experiences and resistance
   in the management of Rural Education
SO REVISTA BRASILEIRA DE EDUCACAO DO CAMPO-BRAZILIAN JOURNAL OF RURAL
   EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE rural education; educational policies; narrative research in education
AB This article presents an excerpt of a study developed within a Master's program in Education, grounded in narrative research. The central objective is to analyze, from the biographical-narrative perspective of a rural school principal in the state of Paran & aacute;, the repercussions and contradictions of contemporary educational policies in the daily routine of school management and rural teaching. The study highlights that such policies are more pernicious for the specific context of rural areas, given the greater precariousness of infrastructure and teacher availability. Narrative research aims to value the subjects' perspective in their daily practices, and how, in this case, this perspective elucidates how policies are received in the school. The interviewee specifically addressed the High School Reform and the teaching career, and, based on this thematic field, three categories emerged: changes in educational policy; how they are received by teachers; career plan and employment contract. It is concluded that there is no dialogue between policies and subjects, nor is there a direct reflection between the written text of the law, its intentions, and how these legal texts are received and implemented, given the mediation of the subjects of educational practices.

TI Management of post-COVID-19 conditions: development and validation of
   educational tools for healthcare professionals
SO REVISTA IBERO-AMERICANA DE ESTUDOS EM EDUCACAO
LA English
DT Article
DE COVID-long; health education; health professionals; educational
   technology; health technology assessment
AB The objective of this study is to describe the process of constructing and validating a guide and infographics designed to guide healthcare professionals in the management of individuals with postCOVID-19 conditions. This is a methodological study developed in two phases: production-construction and semantic validation of the technologies. Phase one comprised situational diagnosis, narrative review, and construction of the educational technologies. In phase two, the technologies were validated by the target audience (nurses and physicians, n=10) using a questionnaire. A minimum semantic validity index (SVI) of 0.80 was considered. The construction of the technologies was based on situational diagnosis and a narrative literature review. The guide and infographics produced present the management of the main post-COVID-19 conditions (dermatological, neurological, cardiovascular, respiratory, musculoskeletal, and gastrointestinal), obtaining an SVI of 0.99. The construction of technologies based on scientific evidence and adapted to the needs of the target audience, followed by validation, ensures clarity and suitability of the materials for the target audience regarding the management of post-COVID-19 conditions.

TI Design Thinking Pedagogy: Tools and Strategies for Engaged Learning
SO TEACHING & LEARNING INQUIRY-THE ISSOTL JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE design thinking; engaged learning; educational workshops
AB Faculty and students have diversified and refined design thinking over recent decades, and more institutions are using it in the development of transformative learning experiences. The first of its kind, this study examines the potential outcomes of design thinking educational workshops, through which students learn and practice design thinking methods. Tailored for the promotion of each course's learning objectives, these sessions cover a diverse range of topics and skills. We build upon existing research, backed by over two decades of design thinking literature and five years of data from a university center for design thinking, to share teaching strategies and classroom practices that foster engaged learning. Through a mixed-methods design, this article explores data collected through five years of short-form design thinking "workshop" sessions. We sourced this data from 971 sessions and represents 7,400 individuals' responses for a short survey provided at the end of each session. Findings are compared to research on high impact learning practices for supporting engaged learning environments. Comparative analysis shows that design thinking learning strategies consistently fostered engaged learning environments. From this comparative analysis, we analyzed the various design thinking learning strategies that participants felt were most valuable. Beyond the analysis, this paper will also present the most highly valued pedagogical tools used in these sessions for readers interested in implementing them in a classroom setting.

TI From Stories to Skills: How a Short Fiction Analysis Course Shapes
   Learning and Academic Readiness
SO TEACHING & LEARNING INQUIRY-THE ISSOTL JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE analysis of short fiction course (ASFC); English language and literature
   (ELL); student; readiness; self-regulated learning; scaffolding
AB This qualitative case study explores how an analysis of short fiction course (ASFC) supports learning and academic readiness among first-year English language and literature (ELL) students in T & uuml;rkiye. The researchers gathered data over a semester through teacher observations, weekly student journals (n = 30), and semi-structured interviews with a diverse subset (n = 10). Analysis employed open and axial coding, with researchers' reflexivity and an independent coder improving trustworthiness. Readiness is defined by various scholars as academic and social integration, self-regulated learning, and scaffolding. Results show a shift from basic learning-style preferences to strategic, metacognitive engagement; ongoing yet decreasing linguistic and affective barriers (e.g., vocabulary, symbolism, writing) addressed through scaffolded tasks; increased motivation and sense of belonging within a supportive classroom environment; and improvements in analytical vocabulary, critical reading, and academic confidence. The study demonstrates that genre-specific pedagogy-specifically, the analysis of short fiction-can facilitate first-year students' transition into disciplinary study, integrating the cognitive, affective, and social aspects of readiness. Limitations include a single-institution context and a small qualitative sample. Recommendations include applying ASFC-like, scaffolded approaches across literature curricula and related humanities courses, as well as conducting comparative and longitudinal research on genre-based interventions.

TI Let's Talk About Race: The Use of Virtual Reality in Improving Higher
   Education Students' Understanding of Privilege
SO TEACHING & LEARNING INQUIRY-THE ISSOTL JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE virtual reality; anti-racism; privilege; perspective taking
ID SOFT SKILLS; INTERSECTIONALITY; UNIVERSITY
AB The prevalence of virtual reality (VR) is growing in many educational spaces. Yet while explored extensively in medical science research, there is a need for more studies on VR in educational and social science research. The present study explores the use of VR to teach higher education students about anti-racism content, specifically about privilege. Recognizing privilege is central to learning about anti-racism since it helps people understand each other's social location, intersectionalities, and access to services. We implemented a two-staged mixed-methods research design, with the first stage consisting of a survey design and the second relying on interview data. Participants volunteered either for stage one or for both stages. Twenty-three students participated in stage one, while 11 participated in both stages. The findings reveal that the VR module promoted the participants': 1) layered understanding of privilege; 2) critical reflection on their privilege; and 3) impetus to engage in more advocacy around the misuse of privilege. The findings point to a need for more strategies that specifically detail how to address the abuse of privilege in order to increase people's comfort in conducting this type of advocacy. The research contributes to a growing body of studies on VR's ability to improve participants' understanding of complex humanistic principles, such as privilege.

TI "Pairing is Crucial": Collaborative Reflective Practice and Team
   Teaching for Transforming Learning and Teaching
SO TEACHING & LEARNING INQUIRY-THE ISSOTL JOURNAL
LA English
DT Article
DE collaborative reflective practice; shared teaching; paired teaching;
   team teaching; educator; transformation; higher education
AB In this study, we explore two academics' critical reflective process as they transition from predominantly online solo teaching work into a shared classroom teaching arrangement, including the impact on their teaching approaches and practices. We employed an autoethnographic and action research methodology to facilitate the shift from critical reflection to collaborative action within a purposefully designed shared teaching classroom space. Leveraging Baeten and Simons' five-pronged team teaching model, we articulate the benefits and challenges of shared teaching responsibilities through the practices of adaptability, open communication, emotional intelligence, and the splitting of cognitive load and practical responsibilities. We suggest that the practice of shared teaching paired with a formal collaborative reflective process is central to authentically revealing teaching values and approaches and can form the basis for acquiring new knowledge and transforming effective learning and teaching practices. This serves as a powerful means to enhance educator professional development in order to support student learning in tertiary education.

TI Educational Gaps in Epigenetics: A Cross-Sectional Study of Health
   Sciences Students' Knowledge and Perceptions in Saudi Arabia
SO ADVANCES IN MEDICAL EDUCATION AND PRACTICE
LA English
DT Article
DE epigenetics; epigenetic mechanisms; DNA methylation; gene expression
AB Background: Genetics is a well-known determinant of brain function, behavior, and disease susceptibility. However, epigenetics, which involves environmentally responsive gene regulation (e.g. DNA methylation), remains underappreciated in health sciences education, despite its role in brain development and disease risk. This study assessed the awareness and knowledge of Saudi health sciences students regarding epigenetics and its impact on the brain and behavior. Additionally, knowledge levels were compared across various health science colleges, and gender-based differences were analyzed. Methods: A cross-sectional questionnaire study was conducted among 419 students from four colleges (Medicine, Applied Medical Sciences, Nursing, Science and Health Professions) at King Saud bin Abdulaziz University for Health Sciences, Jeddah, between September 2024 and 2025. Non-probability quota sampling was used. The survey evaluated demographic data, general epigenetic knowledge, and the links between epigenetics, brain, and behaviour. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics (Chi-square/Fisher's exact tests; p<0.05). Results: Females demonstrated greater awareness of "epigenetics" than males (p = 0.001). Males more often believed epigenetic changes were irreversible (p = 0.003) and doubted their heritability (p = 0.046). College of Medicine (COM) students demonstrated the highest level of epigenetic knowledge (p < 0.001), with 39% recognizing its role in gene expression and disease. COM students also identified DNA methylation as a key mechanism (p = 0.004) and agreed that social environments shape brain development (39.6%, p = 0.048). In contrast, College of Science and Health Professions (COSHP) students often disagreed that life experiences affect gene expression (50%). Gender and college-based disparities were evident in perceptions of parenting's epigenetic effects (p = 0.032) and twin studies (p < 0.001). Conclusion: There are notable gaps in epigenetic knowledge among health sciences students, with variations based on gender and college level. Female students demonstrated a greater awareness of epigenetic mechanisms, while male students focused more on the role of research in understanding the social determinants of health. Curriculum reforms should incorporate epigenetics into health sciences programs to address these disparities.

TI Comparative Effectiveness of Ultrasound-Guided Posterior Approach versus
   Landmark-Based Middle Approach for Internal Jugular Vein Puncture in
   Resident Training
SO ADVANCES IN MEDICAL EDUCATION AND PRACTICE
LA English
DT Article
DE ultrasound; internal jugular vein; visualization; hemodialysis
ID VENOUS CANNULATION; CLINICAL-OUTCOMES
AB Objective: To evaluate the teaching effectiveness of bedside ultrasound-guided posterior internal jugular vein puncture in the training of resident physicians. Methods: From March 2019 to June 2024, 24 resident physicians at Taizhou First People's Hospital were randomly assigned to a study group (n=12) and a control group (n=12). The study group received simulation-based training using a Mindray ultrasound skill training system, including repeated practice on a phantom model, followed by supervised patient procedures. The control group received training in anatomical landmark-based middle internal jugular vein puncture with equal practice time. Both groups received 2 hours of didactic teaching and self-study materials. Each physician performed the procedure on three patients, resulting in 36 cases per group. Procedural success was defined as successful guidewire insertion and catheter placement, confirmed by blood aspiration and subsequent chest X-ray. After completing the procedures, resident satisfaction was assessed using a standardized questionnaire. Results: The study group had a 100% success rate, compared to 66.67% in the control group (chi(2)=14.40, P<0.001). First-attempt success rates were 83.33% in the study group versus 41.76% in the control group (chi(2)=13.33, P<0.001). The study group required fewer attempts (1.22 +/- 0.54 versus 1.92 +/- 0.91, t=-3.95, P<0.001), had no arterial punctures (0% versus 19.44%, chi(2)=5.70, P=0.02), and shorter procedure times (4.53 +/- 3.09 versus 7.08 +/- 4.99 minutes, t=-2.61, P=0.01). Resident satisfaction was higher in the study group (100% versus 58.33%, chi(2)=4.04, P=0.01), No pneumothorax, hemothorax, or clinically significant hematoma occurred in either group. Postprocedural chest X-ray confirmed correct catheter tip position in all 72 patients (100%). Conclusion: Short-term training in bedside ultrasound-guided posterior internal jugular vein puncture enables resident physicians to master this technique effectively, demonstrating good clinical application outcomes.
C1 [Yu, Ling'an; Feng, Ziqi; Han, Yingmin; Wu, Xinhong; Zheng, Shouhao] Taizhou First Peoples Hosp, Dept Nephrol, Taizhou, Peoples R China.

TI TEACHING ACADEMIC WRITING IN THE CHATGPT ERA

DT Article

   intelligence
AB Mastering academic writing remains a formidable challenge for university students. DE Coexistence plan; school coexistence; positive coexistence; well-being

AB This article aims to analyse teacher perceptions regarding the relevance of Coexistence Plans within schools that promote positive coexistence, serving as models for the coordination of child welfare and protection.    EDUCATIONAL NEEDS
SO AULA DE ENCUENTRO
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Primary education; inclusion; special education; specific educational
   needs
AB Spain recognizes the right to educational inclusion and is committed to achieving a high-quality, inclusive, and equitable education; however, it remains far from providing it. The existence of a dual educational system-comprising mainstream and special education- the differentiation of students with specific educational needs (SEN) from the rest of the students and the implementation of measures and resources for individualized (isolated) attention, decelerate the progress toward an inclusive education for all students. Within a quantitative methodological framework, a documentary study was conducted to examine the progress made towards inclusion over the last five academic years by analyzing statistical data from the Ministry of Education and Vocational Training's statistics on non-university education. TI COMPARISON OF BULLYING IN TWO GROUPS OF SECONDARY SCHOOL ADOLESCENTS
SO AULA DE ENCUENTRO
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Bullying; health status; adolescent; Comparative study
AB The repeated abuse of power by an individual or a group over others is recognized as bullying. An investigation was conducted with the aim of comparing bullying across two groups of secondary school students from two educational institutions in the Coastal Region of Ecuador. Adopting a quantitative approach and a non-experimental design, the study involved 283 students (160 from school I and 123 from school II). Data were collected using the School Bullying and Violence Scale. The analysis revealed statistically significant differences in the factors of intimidation and social exclusion (p=0.000). The predominant means for both bullying factors and health-related impact fell within the "verified" and "well-verified" categories. Overall, significant differences were identified between the two groups.

TI MOTIVATION AND READING COMPREHENSION IN "THE LITTLE PRINCE": A
   COMPARISON BETWEEN PRINTED BOOKS AND AUGMENTED REALITY
SO AULA DE ENCUENTRO
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Reading skills; reading comprehension; reading motivation; augmented
   reality; educational technology
ID EDUCATION
AB This quasi-experimental study analysed the effect of using Augmented Reality (AR) versus the printed format on the motivation and reading comprehension of seventh-grade students in Chillan, Chile. The sample consisted of 54 students: an experimental group that read The Little Prince using AR and a control group that worked with the printed format. Validated instruments were administered to measure motivation and reading comprehension across three levels (literal, inferential, and critical), supplemented by a structured observation guide. These findings suggest that AR can be a promising pedagogical tool when integrated with didactic intentionality and curricular alignment.

   Achievement in Kosovo Higher Education

DT Article

AB This study examined how university students' multilingualism, growth mindsets, experiential learning preferences, and self-regulation strategies were associated with academic achievement in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) and non-language subjects in Kosovo higher education. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 170 undergraduate students. Data were collected through validated measures of language mindset, self-regulation, and experiential learning preferences, together with a self-report multilingual proficiency index based on the number of languages participants reported using at an advanced level.    Armenian English as a Foreign Language

ID 2ND-LANGUAGE
AB This study investigated the acquisition of personal and impersonal passive constructions among Armenian English as a foreign language (EFL) learners, focusing on the intersection of linguistic transfer and pedagogical practice. While research has extensively covered passive voice acquisition in various L1 backgrounds, Armenian learners have remained underrepresented in the literature. TI Vlogging to Improve Authentic Speaking in an English Course for Business
   Management
SO IAFOR JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE authentic oral production; EFL speaking; English for Specific Purposes
   (ESP); formative feedback; speaking anxiety; vlogging
AB This teaching practice research examined the pedagogical effects of integrating a recurring three-task cycle-vlog, or video log, creation, peer written feedback, and teacher-student conferences-into an English course designed primarily for Business Management. The study aimed to explore how structured vlog-based authentic oral production influenced English for Foreign Language (EFL) learners' English-speaking proficiency, confidence, and learning motivation. Participants were 57 sophomore students majoring in business-related fields at a university in Taiwan. A mixed-methods approach was employed over one academic semester. Quantitative data included scores from speaking pre-and post-tests, individual video-recorded presentations, and final in-class group presentations. Qualitative data were collected through vlog evaluators' feedback, instructor field notes, student end-of-semester reflections, questionnaires, and semi-structured interviews. Results indicated that repeated engagement in three vlog cycles led to noticeable improvements in students' speaking fluency, discourse organization, and confidence in oral expression. However, challenges remained in pronunciation accuracy and spontaneous delivery. Overall, the findings suggest that embedding vlogging within a structured instructional cycle can effectively foster authentic oral production and support speaking development in EFL practice-oriented courses. The study offers practical implications for EFL instructors designing speaking tasks and activities for language learners in various fields.

DE convergent mixed-method; English language teaching; English learners

AB Research worldwide is increasingly documenting how schools and teachers respond to multilinguals' linguistic repertoires through translanguaging pedagogies that affirm students' languages and identities. Yet, scant empirical evidence examines how translanguaging works in multilingual contexts with indigenous learners in Asian countries. This work is theoretically framed by pedagogical translanguaging, particularly in relation to teacher-led strategies designed to support academic content mastery among English learners. Using convergent mixed methods that included surveys, interviews, focus group discussions, and observations of teachers' instructional approaches in northern Philippine classrooms, this study captured teachers' dispositions and perspectives. The pedagogical implications of this study inform recommendations for practitioners on asset-based instructional paradigms for teaching multilingual English learners.

TI Comparing One-Way and Two-Way Listening Strategies of University English
   Learners in General and Specific English Contexts
SO IAFOR JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE EFL learners; English for general purposes; English for specific
   purposes; listening strategies; one-way listening; two-way interactive
   listening
ID METACOGNITIVE AWARENESS; QUESTIONNAIRE; INSTRUCTION
AB Listening is a strategic and context-sensitive skill, yet research has predominantly examined strategy use in non-interactive listening with limited attention to how learners adapt strategies across one-way and two-way listening in different instructional contexts. This mixed-methods study investigated differences in listening strategy use among 384 Taiwanese university students enrolled in English for General Purposes (n = 195) and English for Specific Purposes (n = 189) courses and examined relationships between strategies used in one-way and two-way listening. Participants completed a modified questionnaire adapted from two established listening strategy instruments. Semi-structured interviews with 20 participants were analyzed to contextualize quantitative findings. Correlation analyses further revealed strong positive relationships between key strategies across listening modes, suggesting an interconnected strategic repertoire. Interview findings indicated that instructional orientation and communicative demands shaped learners' strategic choices. These findings highlight the importance of differentiating listening instruction according to interactional demands and course contexts and contribute to a more context-sensitive understanding of strategic listening development in an English as a foreign language setting.

TI Academic Lecturers' Perceptions of English as a Lingua Franca in the
   Eurasian Context
SO IAFOR JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE English language education; English as a Lingua Franca; awareness of
   English as a Lingua Franca; intensive English language curricula
AB English has traditionally been taught as a foreign or second language. However, the rise in nonnative speakers confirms its status as English as a Lingua Franca (ELF). As universities evolve into multicultural hubs, the perception of English significantly shapes pedagogical approaches. This study investigated intensive language program curricula and materials, specifically evaluating how lecturers perceived the role of ELF within their academic contexts. While existing literature mainly targets primary and secondary education, this research incorporated cross-cultural perspectives by selecting five public university lecturers from Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Croatia, Hungary, and Turkey. Adopting an in-depth qualitative case study method, semi-structured interviews were conducted centered on three lesson plans, each incorporating elements of various English(es). Four main themes consisting of materials, practices, exercises, and assignments were identified and analyzed using MAXQDA software. The findings revealed a geographic divergence in pedagogical preferences. Participants from Turkey, Bulgaria, and the Czech Republic demonstrated a greater inclination toward implementing ELF-oriented lesson plan, whereas lecturers from Croatia and Hungary favored a second language-oriented approach. Interestingly, despite varying levels of openness, none of the participants expressed an interest in fully adopting a purely ELF-based lesson plan. The demand for high-level academic skills and the dominance of foreign materials restricted the implementation of ELF-based practices in higher education. However, a consensus emerged on prioritizing communicative competence and diverse accents to reflect the global reality of English. This study highlighted the need for flexible curricula bridging the gap between formal accuracy and practical usage.

TI Learner Engagement and Confidence in Mixed-Ability University English as
   a Foreign Language Classrooms: A Teacher-Centered Analysis with Student
   Perspectives
SO IAFOR JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE affective factors; EFL teaching practices; English as a Foreign
   Language; learner engagement; learner confidence; mixed-ability
AB Mixed-ability instruction is a common feature of university English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classrooms in Japan, yet it presents challenges for promoting equitable participation and positive affective experiences among students with differing proficiency levels. Two key dimensions of this challenge are learner engagement, reflecting active participation, and learner confidence, reflecting students' self-perceived competence. In mixed-ability contexts, these dimensions may not develop in parallel. This study examined the extent to which engagement and confidence functioned as distinct yet interrelated dimensions in mixed-ability Japanese university EFL classrooms. A qualitative-dominant mixed-methods design was adopted, integrating semi-structured interviews with 25 instructors, classroom observations, and a student perception survey administered to one mixed-ability class (N = 28). Qualitative data were analyzed thematically, and quantitative survey data were analyzed descriptively and exploratorily to examine relationships among engagement, confidence, and perceived inclusion. Quantitative results indicated that engagement was strongly associated with perceived inclusion (r = .71, p < .01) and remained relatively high across proficiency levels. Confidence, however, showed greater variability and was closely linked to self-perceived proficiency, with large effect size differences between lower and higher proficiency students (d = 1.27). Exploratory regression analysis further showed that perceived inclusion accounted for additional variance in engagement beyond confidence (R2 = .55). These findings suggest that engagement and confidence are separate but interrelated affective dimensions. Engagement was more closely associated with perceived inclusion, while confidence was linked to self-perceived proficiency. The study emphasizes the exploration of affective processes shaped by instructional practices rather than causal relationships. This highlights the importance of classroom practices that foster inclusive participation and sustained confidence development in heterogeneous EFL contexts.

TI A Correlational Study Between Intertextual Competence and Reading
   Comprehension among Chinese as a Second Language Learners
SO IAFOR JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE CSL learners; intertextual competence; language education; reading
   comprehension; second language acquisition
AB To successfully deal with foreign language discourse, a learner requires a set of competences. The present study employs statistical methods to examine the relationship between Chinese as a second language (CSL) learners' intertextual competence and their reading comprehension ability, namely Pearson correlation. In addition, it explores whether exposure to the target language environment outside the classroom influences these variables. The sample of this study consisted of 30 foreign students obtaining their Master of Teaching Chinese to Speakers of Other Languages (TCSOL) in two partner universities: Changchun university in mainland China and Ryazan State University in Russia. According to the language used outside the classroom, the participants were divided into two groups-with and without Chinese language immersion, respectively. Other educational conditions were viewed as common due to a cooperation agreement that required all participants to receive training from educators of the same Chinese university. The data collection procedure included specially designed reading tests with open-ended and closed-ended questions. The participants were asked to read 10 short texts and mark cases of intertextuality, explaining their source and meaning. A set of multiplechoice questions was then used to check their understanding of these texts. The results indicated the existence of a distinct correlation between intertextual competence and reading comprehension, indicated by a .87 Pearson coefficient. Descriptive analysis further proved that the inability to recognize cases of intertextuality resulted in failure to grasp the full understanding of the Chinese text. Moreover, learners exposed to the target language outside the classroom, in a CSL format, had a significantly higher level of intertextual competence. This suggests the need for classroom activities to facilitate intertextual competence development for the learners lacking such an environment.

TI Preserving Local Cebuano Vocabulary: Pedagogical Responses to Language
   Shift Challenges

DT Article
DE culturally responsive pedagogy; educational language policy; language
   preservation; lexical attrition
AB This study explored the importance of preserving local Cebuano vocabulary in an upland community in Cebu Province, Philippines. It aimed to mitigate the language shift caused by globalization, urbanization, modernization, and the focus on English and Filipinos in schools. A total of 148 local words were identified through archival research and interviews. These words were grouped into six categories: Agriculture, Food, and Livelihood; Domestic Life and Household Practices; Social Relations, Community Life, and Built Spaces; Traditional Tools, Technologies, and Material Culture; Environment, Geography, and Local Ecology; and Beliefs, Rituals, and Cultural Expression. Moreover, this study urges the inclusion of the Cebuano vocabulary in the curriculum to enhance learning and protect community heritage. Integrating local vocabulary is vital for sustaining language skills and supporting relevant education.

TI Stories of struggle and strength: Impact of multigrade teaching on
   primary teachers' wellbeing in rural Pakistan
SO ISSUES IN EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
ID SCHOOLS
AB Multigrade teaching is a prevalent feature in schools situated in underprivileged rural regions globally, primarily attributable to insufficient infrastructure, a shortage of qualified teachers, and geographic dispersion. This study aims to examine the impact of multigrade teaching on teachers' wellbeing in Balochistan, Pakistan, and to explore how these teachers experience, interpret, and maintain their well-being amid challenges such as professional isolation, resource constraints, and systemic issues. TI University research in the Bicol Region, Philippines: Topic choices,
   dissemination, and ranking metrics
SO ISSUES IN EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
ID HIGHER-EDUCATION
AB The quality of universities' research dissemination efforts underpins how knowledge is shared, accessed, and applied, shaping its contribution to socially responsive, locally relevant, and sustainable development. Using a descriptive-documentary design, and ranking indicators (AD Scientific Index and EduRank) were analysed across nine state-funded universities and colleges in the Bicol Region, Philippines. AB Thousands of private autonomous institutes serve millions of learners in Iran, yet their managerial practices remain largely unexamined. TI Secondary school agricultural education in New South Wales: A foundation
   for university study of agriculture
SO ISSUES IN EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
AB Following previous analyses of enrolment and graduation patterns in secondary agricultural education in Australia (Graham et al., 2025), this paper presents a detailed study focusing on Australia's most populous state, New South Wales. It shows that Year 12 secondary student completions of both the Higher School Certificate (HSC) Agriculture and HSC Primary Industries courses have been steady over time. They are much higher in number in rural/regional areas despite the very much larger student population residing in Sydney. This plateau in enrolments, despite a significantly rising population, equates to a per-capita decrease in secondary students studying agriculturerelated courses over the period 2011-2022. The number of schools offering the courses to completion in NSW has remained steady, although only 9% of Sydney secondary schools offer these subjects. Further, 17.9% of all HSC Agriculture completions in Sydney from 2011-2022 came from only two schools, and 47.9% came from just ten schools in that city. Sydney-based secondary students are also significantly underrepresented in first preferences for agriculture-related tertiary degrees. Data show that whilst some of these Sydney students are preferencing agriculture courses at university in their top five, it is less likely to be first preference, compared with rural/regional student preferences. Given that so few Sydney schools offer agriculture and that those studying agriculture courses at secondary school are around ten-times more likely to first preference agriculture-related degrees than those who do not, it seems that increasing the metropolitan offerings and attractiveness of the subject at secondary level should have significant upside for higher education enrolments and graduate numbers.

TI A sociocultural exploration of EFL lecturers' PD for supporting
   scholarly writing in Indonesia
SO ISSUES IN EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
ID TEACHER EDUCATORS
AB Professional development (PD) has become increasingly vital for English as a foreign language (EFL) lecturers who teach writing for scholarly publication (TWSP) in Indonesian higher education. While academic publishing has gained growing prominence as a key indicator of institutional and individual success, limited research has examined how PD supports EFL lecturers in developing the pedagogical and scholarly competencies required to teach writing for scholarly publication effectively. Addressing this gap, our study explores Indonesian EFL lecturers' lived experiences of PD in TWSP from a sociocultural perspective. Drawing on Barkhuizen's (2008) narrative inquiry framework, the data were collected through narrative frames and in-depth semi-structured interviews with five purposively selected lecturers. Thematic analysis of the narratives identified six major PD activities: engagement in communities of practice, self-initiated professional participation, collaborative and mentorship-based teaching, reflective practice, collaborative academic writing, and pursuit of doctoral education. The findings also revealed four key impacts of PD: enhancement of professional knowledge and skills, improvement of student learning outcomes, development of reflective teaching practices, and expansion of professional networks. This study contributes to the underexplored area of PD in teaching scholarly writing within Indonesian higher education and provides practical insights for designing targeted, sustainable PD programs that support EFL lecturers' academic and pedagogical advancement in both local and international contexts.

TI What are information literacy skills? Western Australian primary
   teachers' interpretations of the ICT curriculum
SO ISSUES IN EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
ID EDUCATION
AB Teachers must equip students to navigate an increasingly complex world of unique challenges and opportunities, necessitating the development of a diverse range of transferable skills. These skills are embedded in the General Capabilities (GC) of the Australian school curriculum. Upper primary school teachers' interpretations of one of the GC, Information and Communication Technology (ICT) learning progressions, was examined, as these skills have become increasingly important with the rise in generative and assistive artificial intelligence. TI Professional development for university academic staff: A longitudinal
   study of course impact and educator growth
SO ISSUES IN EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
ID TEACHERS; LEADERSHIP; PROGRAM
AB Universities invest significantly in professional development for teaching staff, yet questions remain about the long-term value and impact of such initiatives. This paper presents findings from a longitudinal mixed-methods study evaluating a ten-week professional development course for university educators, conducted between 2020 and 2024. Drawing on adult education and professional development theory within the context of academic development in higher education, our study explored which course elements participants identified as contributing to successful outcomes and examined the sustained personal and professional impacts. This study contributes to the evidence base supporting strategic investment in professional development and highlights the importance of designing inclusive, reflective, and practice-oriented learning experiences for higher education professionals.

TI The paradoxical nature of vandalism in Malawi's mission secondary
   schools: Countering deep disconnects
SO ISSUES IN EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
AB Despite their reputation for upholding high moral and spiritual standards, mission schools in Malawi are paradoxically experiencing alarming rates of vandalism. This study explores the paradox of learner-perpetrated vandalism within these specific educational contexts, with a focus on their nature, causes, and consequences. Adopting a qualitative, phenomenological research design, this study engaged 26 participants - including teachers, former students, and education officials - through semi-structured interviews. Thematic analysis revealed that vandalism manifests as destruction of school, teacher, and church property. Key causes include student frustration with exclusionary school policies, peer pressure, substance abuse, and harsh disciplinary measures that provoke retaliatory actions. The consequences are severe, imposing significant financial burdens on parents and schools, disrupting learning activities, damaging institutional reputations, and leading to punitive legal ramifications for students. Our study concludes that vandalism in mission schools is a symptom of a deep disconnect between institutional ideals and the lived realities of students, requiring a systemic shift towards more inclusive and restorative practices.

TI English teacher recruitment in Thailand: Market ideology,
   native-speakerism, and legitimacy in schools
SO ISSUES IN EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
ID FILIPINO TEACHERS; LINGUA FRANCA; ATTITUDES; EDUCATION; STUDENTS
AB This study presents a theory-building analytic synthesis of research on English teacher recruitment in Thailand's secondary education sector, examining how native-speakerism and market ideology structure legitimacy and reproduce inequities in teacher hiring. Framed as a staffing and governance issue, the synthesis clarifies how legitimacy criteria are specified, audited, and normalised in education labour markets. Drawing on a systematically assembled corpus of 16 published studies, research was analysed as interpretive data to identify convergent evaluative criteria across recruitment discourse, policy analysis, and empirical work. The synthesis indicates that recruitment practices privilege symbolic markers of nativeness, including nationality, accent, and racialised identity, over pedagogical expertise and contextual competence. Simultaneously, competence-based criteria-demonstrated language proficiency, pedagogical expertise, and intercultural competence-recur across the literature but remain analytically fragmented and structurally marginalised within hiring instruments and institutional decision-making. To address this fragmentation, our study theorises the extralocal teacher of English (ETE) as a second-order analytical classification that consolidates these criteria and enables cross-study comparison, independent of nativeness-based labels. By advancing ETE as an analytical construct rather than an empirical recruitment category, our study offers a transferable framework for education research on recruitment inequities in Thailand and comparable schooling systems.

TI Design and technology pre-service teachers' university course lived

SO ISSUES IN EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH

DT Article

AB Design and Technology (D&T) education, historically rooted in industrial and manual arts, now integrates design-focused thinking with the practical processes of prototyping and making. Drawing on a doctoral study, this article examines the university course experiences of ten pre-service D&T teachers in Western Australia and how these shaped emerging beliefs and professional identities. Using an interpretivist framework and interpretative phenomenological analysis, interviews with ten final-year pre-service teachers were analysed. These insights contribute to strengthening university-based D&T teacher education and preparing reflective, adaptable teachers for technology-rich educational contexts.

TI Reflecting on South Africa's Grade 4 English workbook: Applying a
   gradual release of responsibility model
SO ISSUES IN EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
ID TEACHERS; LANGUAGE
AB Literacy workbooks, a key educational resource in South Africa, often lack a researchbased instructional design, potentially undermining their effectiveness in scaffolding learning. This study evaluated the Grade 4 English First Additional Language workbook using a content analysis framed by the gradual release of responsibility (GRR) model. Activities were analysed to determine the presence and sequence of the four GRR stages: modelling, guided practice, collaborative learning, and independent practice. The analysis revealed a significant misalignment with the GRR framework. Findings showed a substantial over-emphasis on independent tasks and a severe under-representation of the critical scaffolding stages, particularly modelling and guided practice. Furthermore, the sequence of activities was often illogical, with higher-order tasks appearing before foundational ones. The workbook, in its current form, provides inadequate scaffolding for learners. The study concludes that developers must intentionally align workbook design with the GRR model's principles to ensure a balanced progression of support. This alignment is crucial for fostering cognitive and metacognitive development, guiding learners toward autonomy, and ultimately improving literacy outcomes.

TI School climate and teacher commitment for empowering leadership in
   Ethiopia's resource-poor secondary schools
SO ISSUES IN EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
AB Ethiopia has prioritised instructional leadership to address a severe learning crisis, yet student achievement remains low. Our sequential explanatory mixed-methods study investigates this paradox by examining the mechanisms linking principals' leadership to academic achievement in underperforming secondary schools in the Gedeo Zone of Ethiopia. Quantitative data from 180 teachers and archival records, analysed via PLS-SEM, were followed by qualitative interviews. The findings reveal a fully mediated pathway: teachers' organisational commitment fully mediates the effect of principals' instructional leadership on student achievement. Furthermore, fostering a positive school learning climate was the strongest predictor of teacher commitment, significantly outweighing the dimension of managing the instructional program, which was crippled by contextual barriers. The study concludes that in resource-poor contexts, leadership development must prioritise empowering principals to build supportive climates over direct instructional management. This offers a critical refinement to internationally prescribed leadership models for similar constrained educational systems.

TI Links between teacher self-efficacy and pedagogical innovations for
   higher order thinking skills

DT Article

AB Teacher self-efficacy (TSE) predicts attitude towards and adoption of instructional change and curriculum reform initiatives. TI Implementation of Emotional Connection Training in Pediatric Primary
   Care: Mixed Methods Study
SO JMIR MEDICAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE medical education; community pediatrics; developmental-behavioral
   health; early relational health; resident education
AB Background: In 2021, the American Academy of Pediatrics released a policy statement spotlighting the health-promoting and stress-buffering effects of early relational health (ERH) and calling for universal ERH promotion in pediatric primary care. However, little educational content for the observation and promotion of ERH is available, highlighting the need for scalable ERH training modules. Objective: This study aims to investigate the acceptability, feasibility, and impact of the "Lens of Emotional Connection," a self-paced, asynchronous, similar to 45-minute ERH training module codeveloped by Reach Out and Read and the Center for Early Relational Health at Columbia University. The module introduces practitioners to emotional connection, an observable component of ERH, through written and video didactic content and experiential rating of emotional connection in videos of parent-child dyads interacting face-to-face. Methods: The evaluation was conducted by the Carolinas Collaborative. Pediatric providers across 8 clinical sites were invited to participate and responded to embedded pre-post surveys. Focus groups conducted with participants further examined the educational experience. Results: Of 653 invited clinicians, 207 (31.7%) participated in the module. Individual survey responses were available for 44-75 participants, depending on the question. Of responders, 64 out of 69 (93%) reported the module was a good way to learn about emotional connection, and 63 out of 69 (91%) felt the module provided valuable knowledge. Overall, 60 out of 69 respondents (87%) reported satisfaction with the module length, and 36 out of 44 respondents (82%) reported they would recommend this training to other clinicians. Focus groups echoed these findings. Comparison of pre-post data showed the greatest changes were in familiarity with emotional connection (n=75, pre mean 54.20, SD 18.59; post mean 73.99, SD 14.73; Cohen d=1.14; P<.001) and confidence in observing the quality of the parent-or caregiver-infant relationship during well-child visits (n=75, pre mean 55.36, SD 18.49; post mean 74.20, SD 14.07; Cohen d=1.28; P<.001). Suggested areas for improvement included more thorough explanations of specific components of emotional connection identified in parent-child interaction videos, a desire for synchronous live training, and additional content addressing what to do if low emotional connection is identified. Conclusions: In this evaluation of a training module designed to introduce pediatric practitioners to ERH and emotional connection, acceptability among participants was found to be high, with most responders reporting it as valuable and reporting they would recommend it. Statistically significant impact was noted in both perceptions of the importance of information about emotional connection and perceived knowledge acquisition. Feasibility of widespread implementation with voluntary participation, as here, was relatively low, with only a minority completing the module. Critically, Reach Out and Read's commitment to iterative creation, validation, and eventual delivery of ERH training creates a scalable avenue for wide-scale implementation, given the organization's presence in >6500 clinics across the 50 states.

TI The silent Mental Health crisis in schools: why education can no longer
   ignore emotional suffering
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES & PSYCHOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE school mental health; emotional suffering; social and emotional
   learning; adolescent well- being; teacher well-being
AB The contemporary school has become a central psychological ecosystem in which children and adolescents develop not only academic competencies, but also emotional regulation, identity, belonging, resilience, and social functioning. However, educational systems often continue to treat mental health as peripheral to learning, interpreting emotional suffering indirectly through absenteeism, poor performance, disruptive behavior, withdrawal, or lack of motivation. This editorial argues that mental health is not an optional concern in education, but a fundamental condition for meaningful and sustainable learning. Drawing on evidence from school-based mental health promotion, social and emotional learning, adolescent digital behavior, and teacher well-being, the paper calls for a psychologically informed reconfiguration of educational practice. It cautions against both clinical reductionism, which risks medicalizing all distress, and superficial well-being rhetoric, which fails to address structural and relational conditions within schools. Instead, it proposes a whole-school approach grounded in mental health literacy, relational safety, teacher support, multidisciplinary collaboration, digital psychological literacy, and evidence-informed prevention. The central claim is that schools should not become clinics, but they must become psychologically intelligent learning communities capable of recognizing, containing, and responding to emotional suffering before it undermines development and educational achievement.

TI Phenomenology of conflict in the Romanian school
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES & PSYCHOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE phenomenology; educational conflict; school management; organizational
   culture; reflective leadership; hermeneutic dialogue
AB Educational conflict is an inherent dimension of school life, yet it is often approached through administrative and disciplinary frameworks that prioritize control over understanding. This article examines educational conflict in Romanian schools from a phenomenological perspective, proposing a shift toward reflective and dialogical management. Drawing on hermeneutic phenomenology, the analysis integrates lived experiences commonly reported by teachers, students, parents, and school leaders, interpreted through the theoretical contributions of Husserl, Merleau-Ponty, Gadamer, and Ricoeur. Conflict is conceptualized as an emotionally lived and narratively constructed phenomenon. The article argues that when conflicts are addressed through description, dialogue, and reinterpretation, they can become resources for institutional learning, pedagogical innovation, and the strengthening of organizational culture.

TI The inclusion paradox: reconciling parental social aspirations with
   academic pragmatism in contemporary classrooms
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES & PSYCHOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE inclusive education; parental attituses; Special Educational Needs
   (SEN); social inclusion; academic pragmatism; attitudinal ecosystem;
   school-family partnership
ID ATTITUDES; CHILDREN; EDUCATION; STUDENTS
AB This research investigates the integration of students with Special Educational Needs (SEN) into mainstream education, focusing on the perceptual divide between parents of children with SEN and those of typically developing children. Using a quantitative, comparative design, the study analyzed a sample of 284 participants (80.98% female) whose children are enrolled in primary and secondary education (ages 6-14). Data was collected via an online questionnaire assessing teacher competencies, resource availability, and psychosocial benefits. The findings reveal a general axiological openness toward inclusion across both groups. However, significant statistical discrepancies emerged: parents of typical children exhibited more ideological optimism regarding integration feasibility, while parents of children with SEN displayed contextual realism, expressing deeper concerns about teacher training and systemic barriers. Specifically, significant differences were identified in perceptions of teacher preparedness, the concrete impact on academic progress, and the development of empathy within the student collective. In conclusion, while inclusion is validated as a moral imperative, its practical success is contingent upon addressing structural deficits. These results underscore the need for targeted educational policies, enhanced teacher professionalization, and robust multidisciplinary support teams to transition from formal integration to an equitable, sustainable inclusive model.

TI Acting and reacting in turbulent times: online education and digital
   competences of high school teachers
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES & PSYCHOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE online education; digital competences; teaching in pandemic; online
   school experience
AB The online school experience forced by the COVID 19 Pandemic represented an unprecedented challenge for modern education systems, a challenge that has become, for many teachers, a turning point of their careers, in which much of what they knew and did suddenly change. The school gradually moved into the homes of teachers and students, and for many teachers it was the first time they taught in this form. It required adaptation and significant additional effort from all actors involved in the educational area to sustain the continuation of the school. The migration to online teaching was unexpected, with no instructions and few guidelines for what online teaching should be like. In this direction, the current study, undertaken on a statistically representative sample of high school teachers in Romania, analyzed their experience in the context of online teaching. Also, the study addresses the level of digital skills of Romanian high school teachers, analyzing the differences between groups and the influences of teaching experiences on the development of digital skills. The analysis integrated in this proposal brings to the forefront the experience of online education through the analysis of quantitative and qualitative data, combined in a mixed method research design. The results of the study reveal diverse experiences, like, lack of centralized support, increasing working time to support the restructuring of practices or deficient digital skills at the beginning of this period. Our study brings draws attention to the diverse adaptation strategies teachers employed in the new context. Some embraced technology with enthusiasm, leveraging digital tools to enhance engagement and foster interactive learning experiences. Others grappled with the unfamiliar terrain, highlighting the need for targeted professional development to bridge gaps in digital literacy. The experience of online teaching was a significant challenge in many ways for teachers, but it was also a period of learning, adaptation and resilience where teachers effectively developed their digital skills and accessed more than ever before online training activities.

TI The role of procedural strategies and graphical representations in

   graphical representations; simple rule of three; image comprehension;
   unit conversions
ID STUDENTS DIFFICULTIES; KNOWLEDGE; TEACHERS; SKILL
AB This study investigates primary and preschool teacher candidates' performance solve two real-life ratebased mathematical problems: one simple and one complex task. TI Artificial Intelligence vs. traditional tools in design teaching:
   cognitive load optimization, critical reconstruction, and design
   competence enhancement
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES & PSYCHOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE generative artificial intelligence; design education; cognitive load;
   critical reconstruction; human-machine collaboration
AB Generative artificial intelligence (AI) aggravates the "technology-thinking imbalance" in design education under the sustainable development goals 4. Lacking dual-path comparisons between traditional and AI tools on cognitive mechanisms, this study explored associations between tool use, cognitive load (CL) and design quality. A pretest-posttest experiment on environmental design students adopted a residential landscape rendering task. Questionnaire, prompt-word analysis and expert blind review data were analyzed via t-tests and structural equation modeling. The results show the AI path was reduced time pressure (3.25 -> 1.58) and a 23.7-point increase in design rationality. Traditional tools acted as a negative CL mediator, while AI presented positive relations, with critical reconstruction contributing 78.6%. The "Three-Stage Progressive" model integrates resource optimization, critical thinking and design competence, facilitating sustainable design education transformation.

TI The impact of individual study routines and academic success on students
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES & PSYCHOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE study habits; academic performance; self-regulated learning;
   micro-routines
ID HABIT; TIME
AB The study investigates the relationship between the development of a consistent individual study routine and academic achievement among pre-service teachers enrolled in three educational disciplines: History of Ideas and Educational Paradigms, Alternative Pedagogies, and Theory and Methodology of Curriculum. Drawing on self-regulation and habit formation theories, the research explores how sustained engagement across a semester predicts academic outcomes. Findings suggest that the quality of engagement, not merely study time, plays a significant role in academic success, particularly in conceptually integrative disciplines.

TI The role, importance and side effects of artificial intelligence (AI) in
   student learning
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES & PSYCHOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE digital technologies; AI; challenges; student learning
AB In recent decades, the rapid development of digital technologies has profoundly transformed the educational process. TI From self to teacher identity: investigation of internal and external

LA English
DT Article
DE teacher identity; dialogical self theory; teacher candidates; self
ID DIALOGICAL SELF; EDUCATION
AB Teacher identity is a dynamic, multidimensional construct shaped by personal, social, and institutional factors. This study uses Dialogical Self Theory (DST) to examine teacher candidates' internal and external self-positions across 14 undergraduate programs. Data were collected from 345 participants using an adapted Personal Position Repertoire (PPR) instrument. Internal positions were grouped into personal, learning environment, teaching profession, social belief, and personal belief domains, while external positions included family, peers, instructors, classmates, and practicum contexts. TI The interplay between work-family and family-work conflict during the
   Covid-19 pandemic in Air Force service members
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES & PSYCHOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE family-work conflict; work-family conflict; work-related rumination;
   Covid-19 rumination; military organizations
ID CONSERVATION; RESOURCES; RUMINATION; RESPONSES; MILITARY
AB This study examines the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on work-family dynamics among military personnel, a context underexplored in existing research. Using a cross-sectional survey of 316 Air Force members with retrospective assessments, we investigated how changes in family-work conflict (FWC) related to changes in work-family conflict (WFC), and the role of work-related and Covid-19 rumination in predicting WFC. Results indicate that the pandemic increased FWC, which in turn led to higher WFC. These findings suggest a sequential process whereby pandemicrelated stressors and cognitive preoccupations exacerbate interrole conflict. The study contributes to understanding the family-work interface during crisis conditions, mainly in military settings.

TI Empathy beyond experience: attitudes toward animals and belief in animal
   mind under controlled pet ownership
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES & PSYCHOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE moral reasoning; moral psychology; human-animal relations; attitudes
   toward animals; animal empathy; belief in animal mind; mediation
   analysis; pet ownership
ID VIOLENCE; HUMANS
AB This study examined associations between attitudes toward animals, animal empathy, and belief in animal mind (BAM), controlling for pet ownership. Adults (N = 288) completed the Attitudes Toward Animals Scale, short Animal Empathy Scale, and BAM scale; ownership was a binary covariate. Correlations and mediation (MLE) were conducted. Attitudes correlated with empathy (r = .261) and BAM (r = .228), and empathy with BAM (r = .226), all p < .001. Empathy partially mediated the attitudes-BAM link (indirect beta = .046, p = .012; direct beta = .170, p = .004). Pet ownership predicted attitudes (beta = -.432, p = .002) but not empathy or BAM. The findings suggest that animal-mind attribution is partly shaped by empathic-attributional processes that remain significant beyond pet ownership. Overall, BAM appears to function as an affective-cognitive construct linked to attitudes and empathy rather than to direct animal contact alone.

DT Article

ID EDUCATION
AB The purpose of this study is to examine the effect of an intervention program in teaching geometry on math anxiety, self-efficacy, and geometry achievements of 5th-6th grade students. The study was conducted during the 2023-2024 school year. The intervention program integrates everyday situations and emotional tools into geometry classes. The intervention program was validated in a pilot phase before the main investigation. TI Psychological stress variations according to the presence of nevi in
   female future teachers

DT Article
DE teachers; external stress; intrapsychic stress; nevi
ID QUALITY-OF-LIFE; BEGINNING TEACHERS; SKIN; IMPACT; SATISFACTION;
   EXPERIENCES; RESPONSES; CORTISOL; DISEASE
AB Teachers play a pivotal role in promoting educational equity, facilitating access to education, improving instructional quality, and contributing to broader sustainable development goals worldwide. The present study aimes to investigate whether psychological stress differs according to the presence of nevi across multiple body regions (trunk, upper limbs, and lower limbs) in future women teachers.    self-esteem The mediating role of depression and cognitive emotion

DT Article
DE depression; self-esteem; cognitive emotion regulation; forgiveness;
   anger rumination
ID MALADAPTIVE COPING STRATEGIES; SOCIAL SUPPORT; ANXIETY; FORGIVENESS;

AB Understanding the mechanisms underlying self-esteem is essential for mental health research. This study examined the relationships between anger rumination, depression, forgiveness, cognitive emotion regulation strategies, and self-esteem in 168 Hungarian-speaking adults from Romania (M = 33.8, SD = 13.3). Neither anger rumination nor forgiveness moderated the depression-self-esteem relationship. Furthermore, adaptive cognitive emotion regulation strategies showed a partial mediating effect between depression and self-esteem, indicating a limited protective role. Overall, findings highlight depression as the central mechanism linking anger rumination and self-esteem, while adaptive coping may partially buffer its negative impact.

TI Gender differences in the manifestation of social empathy and tolerance
   of diversity
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES & PSYCHOLOGY
LA English
DT Article
DE empathy; tolerance; acceptance; diversity
ID MODEL
AB The study analyzes the relationship between social empathy and tolerance towards diversity among students, with a focus on gender differences, on a sample of 207 subjects. TI Democracy in the Classroom: 'It's All About Participation'
SO JOURNAL OF TEACHING AND LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
AB This article investigates teachers' conceptions of democracy, citizenship, and participation in Norwegian upper secondary vocational education and training (VET). While there is ample research on students' understanding of democracy, less research has focused on how teachers understand the concept. Democracy and citizenship are among three interdisciplinary topics in Norway's LK20 curriculum, and participation has a central place in both the curriculum and the Education Act, making this study both timely and important in the Norwegian context. This paper examines how the participating teachers understood the concepts of democracy, citizenship, and participation, their teaching of those concepts, and their classroom instruction. This qualitative study draws upon six semi-structured interviews with teachers working in an upper secondary school, whose principal recruited three female and three male teachers of common-core subjects in vocational study programs. The data were analyzed through meaning compression. The findings suggest that teachers view democracy and citizenship as broad, diffuse concepts, yet the concept of participation contributes to making democracy education more concrete and manageable. The study can enhance teachers' understanding of the concepts of democracy, citizenship, and participation, as well as the type of democracy education students receive in their daily experiences.

TI Self-Empowerment and Academic Success: CliftonStrengths in Doctor of
   Physical Therapy Students
SO JOURNAL OF TEACHING AND LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
ID PERFORMANCE
AB Leadership is vital in healthcare, improving patient care through quality, safety, and accountability. This study aimed to identify common CliftonStrengths themes among Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) students, to explore correlations with GPA, and to assess students' perceptions of their strengths. A retrospective, mixedmethods study was conducted with 121 DPT students. CliftonStrengths assessments were administered, and quantitative data were analyzed for common strengths and GPA correlations. Qualitative data explored student perceptions. The most common strengths were Restorative, Achiever, Relator, Learner, and Harmony. Command, Context, Maximizer, and Self-assurance were the least common. Relationshipbuilding was the most frequent domain, influencing the least. No significant correlation was found between strengths domains and GPA, though students in the Executing domain had the highest average GPA (3.41) and those in Influencing the lowest (3.04). Findings align with those of other healthcare studies, in which Learner, Relator, and Achiever are common strengths. Qualitative analysis revealed increased self-awareness and empowerment when reflecting on their identified strengths. Incorporating strengths-based assessments such as CliftonStrengths fosters leadership development among DPT students, aligns with the APTA's vision, and prepares future therapists for effective patient care.

TI Effectiveness of Automation Studio Software in Enhancing Electrical
   Engineering Students' Skills in Designing PLC Ladder Diagrams
SO JOURNAL OF TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND TRAINING
LA English
DT Article
DE Automation studio software; PLC; ladder diagram; electrical;
   experimental
ID EDUCATION
AB The growing complexity of industrial automation requires Electrical Engineering students to develop higher skills in the area of Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) programming, more specifically on ladder diagram design. The conventional methods often lack sufficient interaction, practice, and actual industry exposure for the students. In this regard, this study aims to determine whether or not Automation Studio Software is effective in developing students' abilities in designing PLC ladder diagrams. A quasi-experimental study was conducted with 30 students for each experimental and control class. The experimental class was taught using Automation Studio, whereas the control class used conventional method of teaching. The instruments included a validated performance test and a student perception survey questionnaire. Results show a significantly improved post-test score for the experimental class by 40.96%, with an N-Gain of 74.96% which falls under moderate category and a very large effect size. Students' perceptions were overwhelmingly positive, 87% reporting enhanced understanding and 92% recommending the integration of the software in the curriculum. This implies that Automation Studio Software presents an industry-based learning environment that is capable of bridging the gap between theory and practice, improving student PLC programming competencies.

DT Article

   Quadrant (LEIQTM); TVET
ID EDUCATION
AB Emotional engagement plays a crucial role in shaping learning experiences, particularly in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), where practical and applied skills require high levels of user interaction. Integrating emotional responses into user experience (UX) evaluation in the digital era is essential for improving web-based learning environments. This research introduces a computer-aided assistive tool to enhance emotional UX assessment using Lokman's Emotions and Importance Quadrant (LEIQTM) model. By automating data collection and processing, the tool provides a systematic and scalable approach to understanding learners' emotional responses. Existing emotion measurement tools struggle to handle large datasets, often relying on manual processes that limit efficiency and accuracy. To address these limitations, this paper presents the design, development, and evaluation of an automated LEIQTM-based assistive tool, comparing its effectiveness with traditional manual methods through qualitative analysis and user testing. Findings indicate that the tool significantly enhances the accuracy and efficiency of emotion assessment, providing valuable insights for educators, instructional designers, and researchers in the education sector. This advancement has broader implications for UX practitioners, technology developers, and researchers, offering a scalable solution for integrating emotional intelligence into digital learning environments. By refining the LEIQTM assessment process, this research contributes to the development of more engaging, responsive, and effective educational tools, ultimately enhancing learning outcomes in vocational and technical education.

TI Gastrodiplomacy as a Cultural Soft Power Strategy: Exploring Indonesian
   MSME Entrepreneurs' Perspectives and Vocational Skill Development Needs
SO JOURNAL OF TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND TRAINING
LA English
DT Article
DE Gastrodiplomacy; cultural soft; power; MSME entrepreneurship; Vocational
   Education and Training; (TVET); culinary diplomacy; Indonesia
ID DIPLOMACY
AB This study investigates Indonesian Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprise (MSME) entrepreneurs' perceptions of gastrodiplomacy as a cultural soft power strategy and identifies vocational skill development needs to enhance their participation in culinary cultural diplomacy. Despite Indonesia's rich culinary heritage, limited awareness and capacity constraints hinder MSMEs from leveraging gastrodiplomacy to penetrate international markets. Employing a mixed-methods approach with 22 culinary MSME entrepreneurs in Garut Regency, West Java, this preliminary study utilized structured questionnaires and semi-structured interviews analyzed through descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. Findings reveal a paradox: while only 31.8% of respondents were familiar with gastrodiplomacy concepts, 77.3% expressed strong interest in learning, and 100% recognized the need for specialized vocational training. Despite low conceptual awareness, 54.5% already engaged in intuitive cultural promotion activities through social media and local collaborations. Key barriers include complex export regulations (68.2%), limited market information (63.6%), and high costs (59.1%). Comparative analysis with successful gastrodiplomacy programs in Thailand ("Kitchen of the World") and South Korea ("Hansik Globalization") highlights the potential for Indonesia to systematically leverage its culinary diversity. The study proposes a comprehensive vocational skill model integrating gastrodiplomacy theory, digital marketing competencies, export navigation, and cultural branding strategies. These findings provide empirical foundation for policy interventions supporting MSME capacity building in gastrodiplomacy, contributing to national soft power enhancement and sustainable economic development through cultural diplomacy.

TI Enhancing Teaching Skills Through Electronic Resources: A Study with
   Prospective Primary Teachers
SO JOURNAL OF TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND TRAINING
LA English
DT Article
DE Pre-service teacher education; classroom management; digital; pedagogy;
   electronic resources; teaching skills
ID EDUCATION; ONLINE
AB The growing recognition of the potential of electronic resources to support pedagogy in teacher education highlights the importance of empirical research, particularly within developing educational systems such as Kazakhstan. This study examines the association between the use of electronic resources and teaching skills, reflective practices, and classroom management competencies among prospective primary school teachers. A quasi-experimental pre-post-test design was employed with a sample of 154 pre-service teachers from two Kazakhstani universities. The findings indicate that participants who used electronic resources demonstrated higher post-test scores in instructional planning and used more adaptive classroom management strategies than those receiving traditional instruction. These results suggest that digital tools may support the development of core competencies in teacher preparation, particularly in under-researched educational contexts. However, the use of nonequivalent groups drawn from different institutions represents a key limitation and warrants cautious interpretation of the findings. The study offers practical recommendations for curriculum developers aiming to integrate traditional and digital pedagogical approaches.
